title: Thesis Meeting 13.07.2026
text:
New notation

\[
\mathcal{L}(T,\lambda,\alpha,\beta)
= \sum_{ij}\Big[T_{ij}\ln\tfrac{T_{ij}}{T^0_{ij}} - T_{ij} + T^0_{ij}\Big] \\
+ \sum_a \lambda_a\Big(\sum_{ij}p^a_{ij}T_{ij} - V_a\Big)
+ \sum_i \alpha_i\Big(\sum_j T_{ij} - O_i\Big)
+ \sum_j \beta_j\Big(\sum_i T_{ij} - D_j\Big)
\]

\[
T_{ij}^* = T^0_{ij}\,\exp\!\Big(-\sum_a p^a_{ij}\,\lambda_a - \alpha_i - \beta_j\Big)
\]
\[
\mathcal{D}(\lambda, \alpha, \beta)
= \sum_{ij} (T_{ij}^0 -  T_{ij})
+ \sum_a \lambda_a V_a
+ \sum_i \alpha_i O_i
+ \sum_j \beta_j D_j
\]
Then denote
\[
\theta = (\lambda_1, \lambda_2, ... , \alpha_1, \alpha_2, ..., \beta_1, \beta_2, ...)
\]
\[
m_{ij} = \big(p^1_{ij}, \dots, p^E_{ij},\; \underbrace{0,\dots,1,\dots,0}_{i},\; \underbrace{0,\dots,1,\dots,0}_{j}\big)
\]
So: \(\log T_{ij}^* = \log T_{ij}^0 - m_{ij}^T \theta\)

title: Thesis Meeting 13.07.2026
text:
Introducing a perturbation
Perturbing the flow on edge a: \[
V_a \rightarrow V_a + \delta V_a
\]
Then the corresponding disturbance in the trip matrix will be
\[
\delta \log T_{ij} = \delta \log \tilde T_{ij}^0 - \delta m_{ij}^T \cdot \theta -  m_{ij}^T \delta \theta
\]
subject to being at new optimum:
\[
\nabla D = 0
\]

title: Thesis Meeting 13.07.2026
text:
Distance Perturbation
\[
\frac{\partial d_{a'}}{\partial V_{a'}} = - \frac{1-P_{a'}}{V_{a'}}
\] For edges e from same origin: \[
\frac{\partial d_{e}}{\partial V_{e}} = \frac{P_{a'}}{V_a'}
\]
What about distances over a path? \(\rightarrow\) Discontinuity

title: Thesis Meeting 13.07.2026
text:
Logit route effective distance
We have the logit route choice probability as
\[
\pi_r = \frac{e^{-\eta c_r}}{Z_{ij}}, \qquad
Z_{ij} = \sum_{s \in \mathcal{R}_{ij}} e^{-\eta c_s}, \qquad
p^a_{ij} = \sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}_{ij}} \pi_r\,[\![a \in r]\!]
\]
Then define the logit route effective distance as
\[
d_{ij} = -\frac{1}{\eta}\ln \sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}_{ij}} e^{-\eta c_r}
\]
where for sufficiently large \(\eta\), \(d_{ij} \approx\) SPT effective distance.
Intuitively: this is the expected distance between the nodes for the average logit route choice traveller (?). So, slightly larger than most “efficient”.
Then:
\[
\frac{\partial d_{ij}}{\partial d_b} = p_{ij}^b
\]

title: Thesis Meeting 13.07.2026
text:
Logit route effective distance - II
So
\[
\frac{\partial p_{ij}^{a}}{\partial d_b} = - \eta \operatorname{Cov}(1_a, 1_b)
\]
Then
\[
\delta \log T_{ij} = \delta \log \tilde T_{ij}^0 - \delta m_{ij}^T \cdot \theta -  m_{ij}^T \delta \theta
\]
can be written in closed form.

title: Thesis Meeting 27.07.2026
text:
Note: The Prior-Constraints Seesaw

the new formulation of OD pair effective distance conveys information about alternative paths to the gravity model
different regularization settings reveal this:

if regularization parameter \(\sigma\) goes up (less trust in edge flow data), then
logit routing dispersion parameter \(\eta\) goes down (allow more alternate paths)
gravity penalty parameter \(\beta\) goes up (more trust in logit effective distance)
inference quality stays very similar after calibration, even though constraints are used less in optimization

section: One last idea: how does uncertainty propagate?
text:
One last idea: how does uncertainty propagate?
The perturbation analysis gives us the perturbation of the transport matrix \(\frac{dT}{dV}\), as well as the perturbation of the OD effective distance \(\frac{\partial d_{ij}}{\partial d_b} = p_{ij}^b\) .
From this, it is possible to model

the variance in est. of T, based on characteristics of noise on edge measurements
the uncertainty in arrival time, based on characteristics of noise on edge measurements, since \[ t_{arrival}(i, j) \propto d_{ij}^{eff} \]

title: Origin, Destination, Contagion
text:
Motivation
Origin-destination travel patterns are important for disease propagation.
OD data is rare. Usually, we have access to data about flows of passengers on edges.

title: Origin, Destination, Contagion
text:
Project Goals
Given the world air transportation network, with
countries as nodes and
existing passenger flight links as edges:

How well is it possible to infer the Origin-Destination matrix of a transport network given only edge flows?
How do OD travel patterns react to a perturbation of flows on an edge? (e.g.: if I cut half of the flights from A to B, which Origin-Destination pairs are affected, and how?)

title: Origin, Destination, Contagion
text:
OD matrix inference: How?

Effective distance:

\(d_{ij} = 1 - \ln {P_{ij}}\) , where \(P_{ij}\) is the fraction of node i’s total outflow that goes to j. Higher passenger fraction = nodes are closer.

Logit route choice model: \[\pi_r = \frac{e^{-\eta c_r}}{Z_{ij}},
Z_{ij} = \sum_{s \in \mathcal{R}_{ij}} e^{-\eta c_s}, \qquad
p^a_{ij} = \sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}_{ij}} \pi_r\,[\![a \in r]\!]\] with \(\eta\) the fitted dispersion parameter. Probability to take a path decays exponentially with how much longer it is than the shortest path.
Logit all-path effective distance: \(d^A_{ij} = -\frac{1}{\eta}\ln \sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}_{ij}} e^{-\eta c_r}\)
Gravity model: \(T^0_{ij} \propto \frac{M_i M_j}{\exp {(\beta d_{ij})}}\)
Inference procedure: find the OD matrix \(T_{ij}\) that is simultaneously closest to the gravity model estimate and closest to fulfilling observed passenger flows on edges according to a route choice model: \(\min (\sum _{ij} p_{ij}^a T_{ij} - V_a)\) for all a.
Mathematically, the quantity to minimize is

\[
\mathcal{L}(T,\lambda,\alpha,\beta)
= \underbrace{\sum_{ij}\Big[T_{ij}\ln\tfrac{T_{ij}}{T^0_{ij}} - T_{ij} + T^0_{ij}\Big]}_{\text{Entropy}} \\
+ \underbrace{\sum_a \lambda_a\Big(\sum_{ij}p^a_{ij}T_{ij} - V_a\Big)}_{\text{Edge flows}} \\
+ \underbrace{\sum_i \alpha_i\Big(\sum_j T_{ij} - O_i\Big)}_{\text{Total outflows}} \\
+ \underbrace{\sum_j \beta_j\Big(\sum_i T_{ij} - D_j\Big)}_{\text{Total inflows}} \\
\]

title: Origin, Destination, Contagion
text:
Perturbation Analysis: How?

Idea: If the described inference procedure is a good data-informed estimator of the OD matrix, then perhaps the estimator’s behaviour at perturbation is a good estimator of perturbation effects in the real network.
Concretely: if the flow V on edge a’ changes (\(V_{a'} \rightarrow V_{a'} + \delta V_{a'}\)), how does the estimated OD matrix change (\(T_{ij} \rightarrow T_{ij} + \delta T_{ij}\))
The perturbation can be calculated in closed form: \[
\delta \log T_{ij} = \underbrace{\delta \log \tilde T_{ij}^0}_{\text{Gravity prior perturbation}} \\ - \underbrace{\delta m_{ij}^T \cdot \theta}_{\text{Routing perturbation}} \\  - \underbrace{m_{ij}^T \delta \theta}_{\text{Optimizer multipliers perturbation}}
\]

title: Origin, Destination, Contagion
text:
Conclusion

It is possible to produce good estimates of origin-destination travel patterns informed by edge flow data using this constrained optimization approach.
Linear perturbation analysis characterizes well the response of the estimated OD matrix, even to large perturbations in flows on an edge.
